def: The log bucket that keeps Admin Activity, System Event, and Access Transparency logs for 400 days. You cannot change its retention, and you cannot modify or delete its sink.
Makes Google personnel get approval from your administrator before they access Customer Data. It needs Access Transparency, and it makes support responses slower.
Defines access levels: conditions on IP ranges, device policy, regions, or identities. VPC Service Controls, IAP, Context-Aware Access for Google Workspace, and IAM Conditions enforce them.
A set of conditions on a request, such as IP range, device, region, or identity, that Access Context Manager defines. Basic levels combine conditions, and custom levels use CEL.
Logs the actions of Google personnel on your Customer Data, with the reason and the accessor's location. It is on by default for every organization at no extra charge.

The portfolio of Google Cloud tools, including Recommender, that give recommendations and insights in value categories such as cost, security, performance, reliability, and manageability. A qualified reviewer must assess a recommendation before you apply it.
A Cloud Armor feature that uses machine-learning models to detect Layer 7 DDoS attacks and suggest WAF rules. A model trains for at least one hour, and a new security policy discards the baseline.
The strategy that client libraries use to find credentials: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then the local ADC file, then the attached service account. The gcloud CLI itself does not use ADC.
An open-source, model-agnostic framework to write agents and multi-agent systems in Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java. The agents run on Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, or GKE.
Audit logs of configuration changes and other admin actions. They are always written, you cannot turn them off, and the _Required bucket keeps them for 400 days with no log charge.
A record of one design decision: the options, the main requirements, and the decision with its reasons. When a decision changes, keep the old one and the reason. Store it near the code.
The exam guide name for a suite of products to build, scale, and govern AI agents. It is now part of Agent Platform, and older questions can also use it to mean Agent Search.
A serverless service that runs ML workflows as a graph of container steps, with no cluster to manage. It records lineage in ML Metadata and has no gcloud commands. Formerly Vertex AI Pipelines.
A fully managed, self-tuning store of data objects with built-in embeddings. Use it when you want vector search without managing indexes, VMs, or replicas.
A fully managed runtime that runs agents in production. It deploys any framework that runs in a container. Sessions keep one conversation, and Memory Bank keeps memory across sessions.
A search engine over your data for search, recommendation, and RAG apps. It gives AI answers grounded in your data, with citations, and it uses the Discovery Engine API. Formerly Vertex AI Search.
A low-code workspace in Agent Platform to prototype prompts and simple agents without code. It compares prompts and models, and it adds grounding with Google Search, RAG Engine, or Agent Search.

Product search and recommendations for retailers, in Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience (GECX). Formerly Vertex AI Search for commerce. Map the Discovery AI need in the Cymbal case study to it.

Google Cloud's integrated system for AI and ML: GPUs, TPUs, networking, and storage, plus open software and flexible consumption options. You do not buy it as one product; you use its parts through Compute Engine, GKE, and Agent Platform.
A PostgreSQL-compatible managed database for demanding OLTP. Its columnar engine runs analytics on live transactional data (HTAP), HA failover loses no data, and read pools scale reads.

A fully managed, pay-per-use gateway for project-level APIs with serverless backends. Each upload of an API definition creates a new API config that you cannot modify. It cannot proxy to Google APIs such as BigQuery.

Google's full API management platform. Its proxy layer adds security, rate limiting, and mediation through policies, plus API products, a developer portal, and monetization. Choose it for partner-facing or high-scale API programs.

An Apigee deployment model where Google runs the management plane and you run the runtime plane on your own Kubernetes clusters. All API traffic stays inside your network, and Pay-as-you-go pricing is not available.
An older serverless platform with a standard environment (language sandbox, scales to zero) and a flexible environment (containers on VMs). Google recommends Cloud Run for new projects.

A registry that groups existing services and workloads from many projects into applications, with owners, criticality, and environment. It organizes resources that already exist; Application Design Center deploys new ones.

A Bigtable setting for how an app routes traffic. Single-cluster routing gives read-your-writes consistency and single-row transactions. Multi-cluster routing gives automatic failover with eventual consistency.

A GA service where platform teams publish approved templates in catalogs, and developers customize and deploy them. It produces Terraform, and App Hub registers each deployed application automatically.
An iPaaS with a drag-and-drop editor and Integration Connectors. Use it to connect, map, and transform data between business systems such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, or Cloud SQL.

A Layer 7 proxy load balancer for HTTP(S). The global external mode gives one anycast IP address for backends in many regions. Only external load balancers are global; internal multi-region designs use the cross-region internal mode.
aws: Application Load Balancer (one per region in AWS)

def: The lowest-cost Cloud Storage class, for data that you keep at least 365 days, such as regulatory archives. Data is available within milliseconds, but retrieval fees apply.

Scans each image for vulnerabilities when you push it to Artifact Registry, then keeps checking images pulled in the last 30 days. Automatic scanning only reports; Binary Authorization blocks a deploy, and On-Demand Scanning can block a build.
The BGP identifier of a Cloud Router or a peer router. Use a private ASN for HA VPN. You cannot change the ASN of a Cloud Router later. Partner Interconnect needs ASN 16550.

Applies a control package, such as EU Data Boundary or FedRAMP High, to a folder. Organization policy constraints and other features then enforce data location, personnel access, and key management controls.
A signed statement that an image finished a required stage, such as a CI build or a QA approval. At deploy time, a Binary Authorization attestor verifies the signature on the image digest.
A CEL expression on a Workload Identity Federation provider. The provider rejects every credential for which it is false. For GitHub or GitLab SaaS, it must accept only your organization's tokens.

A Cloud Storage bucket feature that moves unread objects to colder classes, and back to Standard when read. By default, objects stop at Nearline after 30 days; set the terminal class to Archive to also use Coldline and Archive.
A MIG feature that recreates VMs whose application fails a health check. Use a more conservative health check for autohealing than for load balancing, and allow the probe ranges in the firewall.

Creates Cloud HSM keys on demand when developers create resources, and grants the service agent access. Google recommends it if its keys meet your requirements. You cannot delete keys that it created.
Agent Platform model training with little code, for image and tabular data only. AutoML Text and AutoML Video are shut down, and AutoML requires a managed dataset.
The HIPAA contract that Google signs with you. Accept it before you store PHI. Use only the products that it covers, and do not use Pre-GA offerings unless their terms allow it.
A Cloud Armor policy on a backend service that checks only requests that go to the origin. With Cloud CDN, cache hits never reach it. Put WAF rules and rate limits here.
The load balancer resource that holds the backends, either instance groups or NEGs. Cloud CDN and most Cloud Armor policies attach to backend services, not to forwarding rules.
A managed backup service for Compute Engine instances and disks, Filestore, Cloud SQL, and AlloyDB. Its backup vaults keep backups immutable and indelible until the enforced retention ends.
Dedicated bare-metal servers for specialized workloads such as Oracle, under a BYOL model. You manage the OS, database, backups, patches, and licenses, so it is not a managed database.

Predictions for accumulated data that needs no immediate response. The model needs no endpoint, and the job reads from and writes to Cloud Storage or BigQuery. For Gemini, it is a discounted per-token option.
The dynamic routing protocol that Cloud Router uses to exchange routes with your routers. HA VPN supports only BGP routing. You cannot create new Classic VPN tunnels that use BGP.
A service that loads data into BigQuery on a schedule, for example from Teradata with a migration agent. It cannot move data out of BigQuery.
A BigQuery feature that shares data across organizations without copies of the data. Its former name, Analytics Hub, can still appear in exam questions.
A Pub/Sub subscription that writes messages to a BigQuery table with no subscriber code. Use Dataflow instead when you must window, aggregate, or deduplicate across messages.
A key-value NoSQL database for large amounts of single-keyed data with low latency and high throughput, such as time series and IoT data. It is not relational, so design the row key with care.
Enforces a deploy-time policy on GKE and Cloud Run, so that only images with the required attestations deploy. On Cloud Run, an organization policy must require it, or developers can turn it off.

A Cloud Storage retention policy that stops deletion or replacement of objects before a set age. Locking the policy is irreversible: after the lock, you can only increase it, and the project gets a lien.
Verifiable data about a build: image digests, source locations, build arguments, and duration. Cloud Build does not generate it when a build step runs docker push.

How fast a service uses its error budget. A rate above 1 uses up the budget before the compliance period ends. Cloud Monitoring starting points: fast burn 10x over 1 or 2 hours, slow burn 2x over 24 hours.

You use licenses that you already own and pay Google only for the infrastructure, and you stay responsible for compliance. Windows Server BYOL needs a version released before October 1, 2019, and sole-tenant nodes.
Use of an existing RHEL or SLES subscription on Compute Engine. For RHEL, use the Red Hat Cloud Access feature. Unlike Windows Server BYOL, it does not need sole-tenant nodes.
A group that reviews and approves changes by hand before release. DORA recommends peer review instead of this heavyweight change approval, and the Adoption Framework calls it a tactical practice.
A future reservation of GPUs or TPUs from a date that you choose, for 1 to 90 days. You pay for the full period, and GPU requests start at least 87 hours after you submit them.
On premises, you buy assets up front (CapEx) and depreciate them. In the cloud, most costs are OpEx: you pay when you consume. Some services, such as sole-tenant nodes, can be classified as CapEx.
A peering option outside Google Cloud, like Direct Peering. It gives no access to internal IP addresses and has no SLA, so do not use it to reach VPC networks.

Capture of ongoing changes from an operational database, to stream them to another system. Datastream is a serverless CDC service for analytics, and Database Migration Service uses CDC replication until you switch.
The systems that handle cardholder data under PCI DSS. Put it in a dedicated VPC network with VPC Service Controls, because a system in the same subnet stays in scope.
The expression language for Workload Identity Federation attribute conditions, custom access levels in Access Context Manager, and custom organization policy constraints.

Injecting failures on purpose to find weak points before users do. Prefer staging, add load during the test, measure recovery against the RTO and the RPO, write a postmortem, and repeat on a schedule.
A Speech-to-Text transcription model that works only in the Speech-to-Text V2 API. Google recommends it for voice transcription in Agent Assist, and it or the telephony model fits phone call audio.

An integration style in which each service reacts to events and no service controls the flow. Pub/Sub and Eventarc suit it. It is hard to monitor, so a process that the business must track needs orchestration.
Google's zero trust access product. It adds access levels by device posture and time, access to apps outside Google Cloud, and data loss prevention and threat protection in Chrome.
A Cloud VPN gateway with one interface, static routing only, and a 99.9% SLA. You cannot create new Classic VPN tunnels that use BGP. Use it only when the peer device cannot run BGP.

Security policies on load balancer backend services that add WAF rules, rate limiting, geography rules, and DDoS protection. Edge policies act before the Cloud CDN cache; backend policies see only cache misses.

The Cloud Armor subscription tier (formerly Managed Protection Plus), Paygo or Annual. It adds full Adaptive Protection, threat intelligence, and advanced network DDoS protection. DDoS response support needs the Annual plan.
Records the actions of your own principals on Google Cloud. Admin Activity logs are always on. Data Access logs are off by default for most services. Access Transparency covers Google personnel.

Track actual spend against planned spend and alert at thresholds of actual or forecasted cost. An alerts-only budget never stops spend. To act on spend, send budget notifications to Pub/Sub and run code.

Writes usage, cost, and pricing data to a BigQuery dataset throughout the day. Enable it early: a regional dataset gets data only from the day you enable it, and a multi-region dataset also gets the previous month.

Caching for the global external and classic Application Load Balancers, set on a backend service or backend bucket. It always uses Premium Tier. You cannot enable it with IAP on the same backend service.

Google Cloud's support offering, with four services: Basic, Standard, Enhanced, and Premium. The service applies to all projects in the organization, and only an Organization Administrator can change it.
A code-free, visual service for ETL and ELT pipelines with prebuilt connectors. At run time, it runs each pipeline on an ephemeral Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster.

A managed continuous delivery service that promotes one release through a sequence of GKE or Cloud Run targets. It adds approvals, canary rollouts, verification, analysis, and rollback. It has only standard and canary strategies.
Keeps key material in a supported external key manager outside Google Cloud. Google does not store or cache the keys, so data is unavailable when the external key manager is unavailable.
Cloud KMS keys in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs that Google manages. They use the same Cloud KMS API as software keys but cost more. Choose them when a requirement names hardware protection.
Google's identity as a service product that manages users and groups, without Google Workspace applications. An organization resource requires a Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account.

A managed intrusion detection service that inspects a mirrored copy of the traffic through Packet Mirroring. It detects threats and alerts, but does not block them. Use Cloud NGFW Enterprise to block.
aws: Traffic mirroring with a third-party IDS

def: Private connections from your network to Google Cloud through Dedicated Interconnect or Partner Interconnect. Traffic stays off the public internet, but it is not encrypted by default. Add MACsec or HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect.
Google's managed key service. You cannot view or export its key material. Key rotation creates a new key version but does not re-encrypt existing data.

Software-defined address translation for outbound traffic from VMs without external IP addresses. It is not a proxy VM, and it allows no unsolicited inbound connections. A gateway serves one VPC network and region.

The distributed, stateful firewall service for VMs and supported load balancers. It has Essentials, Standard, and Enterprise tiers. Google Cloud bills traffic at the tier of the features that the rule uses.

The Cloud NGFW tier that adds intrusion prevention, URL filtering, and TLS inspection. Firewall policy rules send traffic to zonal firewall endpoints, which block threats inline. It works only through firewall policies.

The managed service that runs the BGP sessions for HA VPN tunnels, VLAN attachments, and Router appliance. The dynamic routing mode decides if its routes cover one region or all regions. You cannot change its ASN.
A serverless platform that runs containers as services, jobs, and worker pools. Services scale to zero, and a request can run for up to 60 minutes. Google recommends serverless first.

Cloud Run services that Cloud Run builds from your source code. HTTP functions run up to 60 minutes with up to 1,000 concurrent requests per instance, and event-driven functions use Eventarc triggers.

A Cloud SQL regional instance with a primary and a standby in two zones, with synchronous writes. Failover is automatic, in about 60 seconds. The standby serves no reads and does not survive a region outage.
A tool that mounts a Cloud Storage bucket as a file system. It is not POSIX compliant and is not an NFS file system, so do not use it as a POSIX file system or a database disk.
A queue service in which the sender names one handler and controls rate limits, scheduled delivery, retries, and deduplication. Use it for calls to a rate-limited partner API, not for fan-out.
A pre-trained translation API with two editions. Basic accepts API keys. Advanced adds glossaries and regional endpoints, such as the EU, but does not accept API keys.
IPsec tunnels between your network and a VPC network, or between VPC networks. Choose it for lower cost, lower bandwidth, or migration tests. By itself, it does not reduce egress costs.
A GKE Standard feature that adds and removes nodes in a node pool. It reacts to Pods that cannot be scheduled and to resource requests, not to actual node utilization.
Encryption keys that you create and control in Cloud KMS. The service agent of the service uses the key, and the key must be in the same location as the resource that it protects.

Google's three DR patterns. Cold keeps only backups, images, and IaC templates (RTO over a day). Warm runs part of the stack (RTO an hour to a day). Hot serves production from both sides (RTO minutes).
A Cloud Storage class for infrequent access to data that you keep at least 90 days, such as disaster recovery data. It has a 90-day minimum storage duration and retrieval fees.
The incident role that is the public face of the response. It sends periodic updates to responders and stakeholders and can keep the incident document current. It reports to the Incident Commander.

Gives you Google Cloud ISO/IEC certificates and SOC reports at no additional cost, and also PCI DSS reports. To share confidential reports outside your organization, you need permission from your sales representative.

Protects data in use, in memory, with a hardware trusted execution environment. Confidential VM protects a whole VM, and Confidential Space lets parties process shared sensitive data that the operator cannot access.

An open source Kubernetes add-on whose custom resources and controllers create and manage Google Cloud resources. Its controllers reconcile continuously and correct drift, while Terraform finds drift only when you run it.

A Network Intelligence Center tool that simulates the packet path between two endpoints from the configuration. It shows the rule or route that drops a packet. A could-be-delivered result does not guarantee delivery.
A US law for online services for children under 13. The Google Cloud COPPA page covers only Google Workspace for Education, so you meet COPPA as the operator of your own service.

An autoscaler that you deploy as a Cloud Run service to scale Cloud Run worker pools, which have no built-in autoscaling. It reads external metrics, such as Pub/Sub backlog, and updates the instance count.
Dedicated physical connections from Google Cloud to AWS, Microsoft Azure, OCI, and Alibaba Cloud, at 10 or 100 Gbps, and 400 Gbps for AWS and OCI. It supports MACsec.
Raw key material that you send with each request. Google does not store it, so you must back up each key. Use it only for Cloud Storage, because CSEK for Compute Engine is deprecated.

A lower price for a 1-year or 3-year commitment. Resource-based CUDs commit to Compute Engine resources in one region and cannot be canceled. Flexible CUDs commit to an hourly spend. A CUD does not reserve capacity.
aws: EC2 Reserved Instances (resource-based) and Compute Savings Plans (flexible)

def: A Cloud Router mode that advertises ranges you choose, with or instead of the subnets. You need it for the Private Google Access VIPs, the Cloud DNS range 35.199.192.0/19, and peered subnet ranges.
A Compute Engine machine shape with the vCPU count and memory that you choose. Only the N and E series and G2 support it, and it costs 5% more than a predefined type.
A minimal-code builder for conversational agents, built on ADK and part of GECX. It is the evolution of Dialogflow CX. Agents use generative playbooks, deterministic flows, or both.
A workflow in Managed Service for Apache Airflow, which you define in a Python file. Airflow DAGs suit batch ETL and ELT pipelines, and they support backfills and re-runs.

Audit logs that record who read data, such as Cloud KMS decrypt calls or Secret Manager AccessSecretVersion calls. They are off by default, except for some BigQuery services, and they have log charges.
A requirement to keep data in a country or region. Enforce it with the gcp.resourceLocations constraint or Assured Workloads. Commitments cover Customer Data at rest, not resource names or labels.
A managed service that runs Apache Beam pipelines for batch and streaming data, with exactly-once processing by default. Use it for new pipelines that need windows, aggregations, or enrichment.
aws: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

def: A serverless CDC service that streams changes from databases such as MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL into BigQuery, Cloud Storage, or Iceberg tables. It does not move a database to a new primary.

Transforms sensitive values so that people and systems do not see the originals. Sensitive Data Protection methods include redaction, masking, hashing, bucketing, date shifting, and tokens that are reversible with the key (AES-SIV, FPE).

Your own 10-Gbps, 100-Gbps, or 400-Gbps circuits to Google in a colocation facility. The multi-region 99.99% SLA needs four connections in two metros, VLAN attachments in two regions, and global dynamic routing.
An IAM policy that stops principals from using listed permissions, whatever their allow policies grant. You attach it to an organization, folder, or project, and IAM checks it before allow policies.

Google's former IaC service, with YAML configurations and Jinja or Python templates. Support stopped on April 1, 2026, and Google turns it down after June 30, 2027. Use Terraform or Infrastructure Manager instead.
Google's earlier conversational agent products, Dialogflow CX and Dialogflow ES. The docs call both legacy. For new designs, use CX Agent Studio, the evolution of Dialogflow CX.
A connection to Google that exists outside Google Cloud. It gives no access to internal IP addresses and has no SLA, so do not use it to reach VPC networks.

The recommended way for Cloud Run to send traffic into a VPC network. Compared with a connector, it has lower latency, higher throughput, and no VM charges. Plan about two subnet addresses per instance.
aws: Lambda function attached to a VPC

def: A Preview tool that converts Deployment Manager configurations and templates to Terraform or Kubernetes Resource Model (KRM) files, for a move to Infrastructure Manager. It does not convert composite types.

A service that migrates MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle into Cloud SQL or AlloyDB for PostgreSQL. Continuous migrations replicate changes for minimal downtime. You cannot undo the cutover (promotion).

A service for document processing pipelines and scanned documents. Its processors extract text, form tables, and RAG chunks, and they extract fields from known document types or your own document types.

A research program that measures software delivery performance. Its four delivery metrics are change lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and failed deployment recovery time. It recommends peer review instead of heavyweight change approval.
A mode that logs what a new policy would deny, but does not deny it. Organization policies, VPC Service Controls perimeters, and Binary Authorization support it. Test in it before you enforce.
A Cloud Storage bucket in two regions with asynchronous replication and automatic failover, with an RTO of zero. Default replication copies 99.9% of new objects within one hour.
A VPC network setting for Cloud Router routes. In regional mode, the gcloud default, learned routes apply only in the region of the router. Multi-region hybrid designs need global mode.
The lowest-cost general-purpose machine series. It offers shared-core types, such as e2-micro, for small low-load apps. It supports custom machine types but not extended memory.

A section of a Cloud Interconnect metro. SLA topologies put connections in different edge availability domains. Google coordinates maintenance between the domains of one metro, but not between metros.

A Cloud Armor policy for global external and classic Application Load Balancers. It runs at the edge, before the Cloud CDN cache and IAP, and can only allow or deny. Put geography and IP blocks for cached content here.
Loading raw data into BigQuery first, then transforming it with SQL. Google recommends this approach for most customers. Dataform or BigQuery pipelines can schedule the SQL work.
The Customer Care service for production workloads. P1 cases get a 1-hour initial response target, 24/7. It has no TAM; the Technical Account Advisor Service is a paid Value-Add Service.

The allowed unreliability: 100% minus the SLO. While budget remains, releases continue. A written error budget policy, approved by product, developers, and SREs, states what happens when the budget is used up.
A pipeline that transforms data before it loads the data into the target. Google recommends ELT for most customers. Teams that want visual, code-free ETL pipelines can use Cloud Data Fusion.

A service that routes events, such as Cloud Storage changes or audit log entries, to targets such as Cloud Run and Workflows. Eventarc Advanced adds a central bus, many-to-many routing, and event transformation.

A Pub/Sub subscription option that works only for pull subscriptions, with subscribers in the same region. Push and export subscriptions do not support it, and publish-side duplicates can still occur.
A Preview service that fails Compute Engine and GKE resources, degrades traffic through a layer 7 load balancer, and fails over Cloud SQL. Its faults stay inside one project and one region.

A store that gives the same features to experimentation, training, and online serving, which avoids training-serving skew. BigQuery tables form the offline store, and Bigtable online serving is the online option that is not deprecated.
A standard format for healthcare records. Agent Search for healthcare searches healthcare records in FHIR data stores.
Managed NFS file storage. Use the Regional tier for resilience to a zone outage; Basic is a legacy tier. Filestore does not serve SMB shares, so use NetApp Volumes for them.
A cost practice that the cost pillar says to adopt, to align cloud spending with business value. The FinOps hub shows savings and optimization opportunities from Cloud Billing and Recommender data.
A US standard for cryptographic modules. Cloud HSM keys use FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs, so choose Cloud HSM when a requirement names that level.
A serverless document NoSQL database with ACID transactions and a MongoDB-compatible API. You cannot change its location or its data access mode after you create the database.
An early workload in a migration that lets the team learn with low risk. Choose one that people use but that is not business critical, with few dependencies and little refactoring.
A Dynamic Workload Scheduler mode that gives GPUs or TPUs for up to 7 days to jobs that can wait for capacity. It uses preemptible quota, but Google does not preempt the VMs.

Minimum Model Armor filters at the organization, folder, or project level. You cannot create a template that is less strict than the floor settings. When floor settings conflict, the lower level wins.
A Cloud DNS zone that sends queries for a domain to other name servers, such as on-premises DNS. The queries come from 35.199.192.0/19, so Cloud Router must advertise that range to on-premises.
A free Google tool that provisions users and groups in one direction, from Active Directory to Google. It does not sync passwords. Users authenticate to Active Directory through SAML SSO.
The EU personal data law. Google commits in its contracts to process your data only on your instructions. You act as the data controller and answer data subject requests.
Google's product that brings shopping and customer service together. It includes CX Agent Studio and AI Commerce Search. Customer Engagement Suite and Contact Center AI became GECX on March 17, 2026.

An AI assistant (Preview) for design, operations, troubleshooting, and cost work in Google Cloud. It has the same permissions as the user. Do not enable it for projects with data residency or CMEK requirements.
aws: Amazon Q Developer in the AWS console

def: An intranet search, AI assistant, and agentic platform for employees. Search results follow each user's permissions, and prebuilt connectors reach systems such as Jira and SharePoint. Formerly Google Agentspace.

Google Cloud's platform to build, deploy, govern, and optimize agents and model-based solutions, with more than 200 foundation models. Google renamed it from Vertex AI in April 2026; the API is still aiplatform.googleapis.com.

A highly compliant, enterprise version of Gemini Notebook that builds a reference point from known, trusted sources. You share notebooks only through IAM roles, never publicly. Formerly NotebookLM Enterprise.

The Google proxies of the global external and classic Application Load Balancers. Instance group and zonal NEG backends must allow ingress from 130.211.0.0/22 and 35.191.0.0/16, and Cloud Armor, not firewall rules, blocks clients at GFEs.
The recommended GKE mode. GKE creates and manages the nodes, clusters are always regional, and privileged Pods are not allowed. General-purpose Pods are billed by their resource requests.
The GKE mode in which you create and manage node pools and pay for the node VMs. Use it only when workloads need privileged Pods or node-level control that Autopilot does not allow.

An API endpoint with no regional isolation, so requests to it can run in any Google Cloud location. It gives no data residency guarantee, so use a regional or US/EU multi-region endpoint for residency.

Google's model to assess cloud maturity in four themes (Learn, Lead, Scale, Secure) and three phases (tactical, strategic, transformational). Use it to evaluate the organization before a migration starts.
A managed file service that supports NFS, SMB, iSCSI, and NVMe/TCP. It is the answer for SMB (Windows) file shares on Google Cloud.

Google Cloud's suite of Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Cloud Trace, Cloud Profiler, and Error Reporting. Monitoring, Logging, and Trace are on by default in each project and collect telemetry for most services automatically.
The VMware platform (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, NSX, and HCX) on Google Cloud bare-metal infrastructure. Teams keep their VMware tools, skills, and processes, so it fits a fast data center exit.

Connecting model output to verifiable sources, such as Google Search, Agent Search, RAG Engine, or your own search API. It reduces hallucinations. Use it for facts that change; use tuning to teach a skill.
The Cloud VPN gateway with two interfaces and dynamic (BGP) routing only. It gives a 99.99% SLA only with a tunnel on each interface. Each tunnel carries 1 to 3 Gbps.
A VMware migration tool that VMware Engine deploys with each private cloud. It moves VMware VMs from on-premises with live, cold, or bulk migration, and the VMs stay unchanged.
A Cloud NGFW firewall policy on an organization or a folder. By default, it is evaluated first, and lower levels cannot override it. The goto_next action delegates the decision to lower levels.

expansion: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
def: A US law for health records. HHS recognizes no HIPAA certification, so accept the Google Cloud BAA and store PHI only in the products that it covers.
A human review step in an AI workflow. Google says that specialized uses that can affect individual rights need meaningful human supervision, and a human-in-the-loop step satisfies this.
A Cloud Storage bucket setting that adds folders and atomic folder operations for AI, ML, and analytics, with up to 8 times higher initial QPS. You enable it only when you create the bucket.
A GKE autoscaler that changes the number of Pods based on CPU, memory, custom metrics, or external metrics such as a Pub/Sub queue size. Do not use it with the VPA on CPU or memory.
Analytical queries on live transactional data in the same database. AlloyDB supports it with its columnar engine, which uses 30% of instance memory by default.
The recommended block storage for Compute Engine. You set performance separately from size. Types include Balanced, Extreme, Throughput, ML, and Balanced High Availability.
A Hyperdisk type that replicates synchronously across two zones in one region, for an RPO of zero in a zone outage. A force-attach to a standby VM takes less than one minute.

Infrastructure defined in declarative, version-controlled files and applied by a pipeline. It gives consistency, repeatability, and easy rollback, and Google recommends Terraform, which finds drift only when you run it.
Rules on a role binding that grant access only when attributes match, such as the request time or a resource tag. You cannot use them with legacy basic roles or with allUsers.

A central authorization layer that authenticates the user and checks an IAM role before a request reaches an HTTPS app, so users need no VPN. IAP TCP forwarding also gives SSH and RDP to VMs with no external IP address.
aws: Application Load Balancer with Cognito, AWS Verified Access

def: A Cloud DNS policy that gives on-premises DNS servers entry points to resolve Google Cloud names. Put it in the VPC network that connects to on-premises; peered and NCC networks cannot reach the entry points.
The incident role that holds the high-level state of the incident, assigns roles, and holds every role that is not delegated. The Communications Lead and the Operations Lead report to this role.
A type of sensitive data that Sensitive Data Protection detects, such as a credit card number. An inspect template lists the infoTypes to look for.

A managed service that runs Terraform in an ephemeral Cloud Build environment and stores the state, logs, and configuration of each revision. Remove backend blocks from its configurations. It does not deploy applications.
The configuration for every VM in a MIG: machine type, image, disks, network, metadata, and provisioning model. You cannot edit a template, so you create a new one and roll it out.
The certification of the information security management system of Google Cloud. Get the certificate from Compliance Reports Manager. It covers Google's part of the stack, not your workload.
An automated phone system that talks with callers. To transcribe IVR call audio, use the Speech-to-Text telephony model or Chirp 3.
The public signing keys of a token issuer. If the IdP has no public OIDC endpoint, upload the JWKS to the Workload Identity Federation provider, up to 8 keys.
A signed token. IAP sends one in the x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion header, and the app must verify it in case someone bypasses IAP.
A control that adds a reason code to each request to use an enrolled key. In some control packages, a policy can approve or deny the request by reason code. It works only with Assured Workloads.
The SDK to use for most Agent Platform Pipelines workflows. Choose TFX instead only when you process terabytes of structured or text data with TensorFlow Extended.
The Google Cloud catalog for data discovery, data lineage, data quality scans, and business glossaries. Google renamed it from Dataplex Universal Catalog in 2026.

The Google Cloud service for open lakehouse data. For most workloads, Google recommends Apache Iceberg tables in the Lakehouse runtime catalog, and BigLake tables let users query an external store without access to it.

A Microsoft Software Assurance benefit that lets you bring server applications, such as SQL Server and SharePoint Server, to Google Cloud. It does not cover Windows Server. A deployed license stays in its region for 90 days.
Compute Engine moves a running VM to another host during host maintenance, and Local SSD data stays. VMs with GPUs and Spot VMs cannot live migrate, so they stop for host events.
A generative model for text, such as Gemini. In CX Agent Studio, generative playbooks let the LLM drive the conversation, and Model Armor screens LLM prompts and responses.

expansion: Letter of Authorization and Connecting Facility Assignment
def: The document that you give to your vendor after you order Dedicated Interconnect. Then you test the connection. Partner Interconnect uses a pairing key instead.

Testing that simulates realistic traffic. Control the rate and the concurrency, confirm that the service scales out linearly, and measure performance at the client. Stress testing pushes the system to its limits to find bottlenecks.
The fastest block storage, for scratch data and caches only. By default, a stop, suspend, or preemption discards the data, and you cannot back it up with snapshots, clones, or machine images.

The Cloud Logging layer that every log entry passes. Its sinks route entries to log buckets, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, or another project. A new sink routes only entries that arrive after you create it.

A serverless way to use Model Garden models: you provision nothing and pay per token or with Provisioned Throughput. Self-deploy instead for custom weights, predictable high volume, or a rule against multi-tenant services.

A Compute Engine backup of a whole instance: its configuration, metadata, permissions, and crash-consistent data from all attached Persistent Disk and Hyperdisk volumes. Local SSD data is not included.

Layer 2 encryption between your router and the Google edge router, on Dedicated Interconnect or Cross-Cloud Interconnect. It does not encrypt traffic inside Google, so Google recommends IPsec and TLS as extra layers.
A managed parallel file system for AI, ML, and HPC with up to 10 TBps of throughput. An instance is zonal. Google makes it the primary choice for AI training checkpoints.
Managed Apache Airflow for batch ETL and ELT workflows written as Python DAGs. It has seconds of latency between tasks, so use Workflows to chain low-latency HTTP calls.
Managed Kafka clusters for existing Kafka workloads. You manage the cluster size and the partitions of each topic. For new streaming workloads, Google recommends Pub/Sub.

Managed Spark and Hadoop with cluster and serverless deployments. Use clusters to migrate existing Hadoop or Spark jobs, and serverless for intermittent Spark jobs. Delete idle clusters instead of scaling them down.
A protocol for agent tool calls. Model Armor can screen tool calls and responses on Google Cloud MCP servers, and Agent Registry lists the approved MCP servers.
The Google Cloud content delivery service for streaming video and large file downloads. It complements Cloud CDN.
An Agent Runtime feature that keeps an agent's memory across sessions. Sessions, in contrast, keep only one conversation.
A managed in-memory key-value service for Valkey, Redis Cluster, and Redis. Replication is asynchronous, so a failover can lose acknowledged writes. Memorystore for Memcached is deprecated.
The list of projects whose metrics one scoping project can chart and alert on. Use a project without resources as the scoping project. Scopes do not move data; metrics stay in their own project.

A group of identical VMs that Compute Engine creates from one instance template, with autohealing, autoscaling, and rolling updates. Google recommends regional MIGs, which spread VMs across three zones by default.
A tool that moves workloads from VMs into containers on GKE, GKE Autopilot, or Cloud Run. It fits web and application servers, not large in-memory databases or licenses tied to hardware.

A lift-and-shift tool that moves VMs from vSphere, AWS, Azure, and VMware Engine to Compute Engine. It replicates disks while the source runs, supports test clones, and needs a short cutover. Rollback is manual.
A platform for asset discovery, assessment, planning, and cost estimates. It groups assets and makes TCO reports from your migration preferences. You choose its data region once and cannot change it.
A group of workloads that migrate together. Rank waves by business value and effort: wave 1 has high value and low effort, and low-value, high-effort workloads go last.

A service that screens LLM prompts and responses for prompt injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data, harmful content, and malicious URLs, for models in any cloud. Inspect-only mode logs violations but does not block them.
A library to discover, test, customize, and deploy Google models, partner models such as Anthropic Claude, and open models such as Llama. An organization policy controls which models people can use.
A service that tracks the quality of tabular models on a schedule or on demand. Use skew detection when you have the original training data, and drift detection when you do not.
The central list of models and versions in Agent Platform. From it, you evaluate a version, deploy it to an endpoint, or run batch inference. An alias is a movable name for one version.
The largest packet size on a network path. Adjust it for protocol overhead; Cloud VPN can need a lower MTU. Do not use HA VPN between VPC networks that need a large MTU.
A balanced general-purpose machine series. It supports custom machine types and extended memory, regional Persistent Disk attaches to it, and sustained use discounts apply to it.
A balanced general-purpose machine series. It does not support Persistent Disk or Local SSD, so it uses Hyperdisk. It supports custom machine types and extended memory.
A pre-trained API for sentiment, entities, entity sentiment, and text moderation against safety attributes.

A global hub with spokes that connects VPC networks, HA VPN tunnels, VLAN attachments, and Router appliance VMs. VPC spokes give transitive connectivity, unlike VPC Network Peering. The hub is control plane only.
A Cloud Storage class for infrequent access to data that you keep at least 30 days, such as backups. It has a 30-day minimum storage duration and retrieval fees.

A load balancer backend that lists endpoints: VM or Pod IP addresses, serverless services, internet or on-premises endpoints, or PSC services. One backend service uses one backend type. The only mix is GCE_VM_IP_PORT zonal NEGs with hybrid NEGs.
A Cloud NGFW firewall policy for VPC networks in one project, global or regional. Unlike VPC firewall rules, it supports secure tags. By default, it is evaluated after VPC firewall rules.

Network troubleshooting tools: Connectivity Tests, Performance Dashboard, Network Topology, Network Analyzer, and Flow Analyzer. Use them to find the rule or route that drops a packet, or to see loss and latency.
Strings on a VM that VPC firewall rules use as targets. Anyone who can edit the VM can change them, so they are not a security boundary. They do not match VMs across VPC Network Peering.
A VMware component that runs in each VMware Engine private cloud, with vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, and HCX. NSX Layer 2 VPN is one of the options to migrate VMs into VMware Engine.
An appliance VM that processes traffic between VPC networks. To insert NVAs in a hub-and-spoke design, use VPC Network Peering, because NCC VPC spokes do not support NVAs between spokes.

Cloud Storage rules that change the storage class of objects or delete them by age, prefix, or version. SetStorageClass moves objects only to colder classes. A bucket with Autoclass cannot also have a SetStorageClass rule.
A Cloud Storage feature that keeps noncurrent versions of overwritten or deleted objects until you remove them. It does not protect against bucket deletion; soft delete does.

A Cloud Logging feature (formerly Log Analytics) that runs SQL on upgraded log buckets, for grouping, aggregation, and joins of log and trace data. Use it when you must count or group; Logs Explorer cannot aggregate.
Text extraction from images and scanned documents. Use Vision API text detection for images at high volume, and Document AI Enterprise Document OCR for scanned documents in a pipeline.
A token-based federation standard. Workload Identity Federation accepts OIDC tokens, for example from GitHub, and Workforce Identity Federation accepts OIDC identity providers.
Artifact Analysis scans that you run with gcloud, locally or in a build. In a Cloud Build pipeline, it can stop a build when the image has vulnerabilities of a set severity.
Predictions for an application that waits for the answer. The model must be deployed to an endpoint, which autoscales replicas and keeps at least one replica in a normal deployment.
The incident role that applies operational tools to mitigate or resolve the incident. Only the operations team changes the system during an incident. It reports to the Incident Commander.
The primary agent for Compute Engine VMs. Without it, you get only basic VM metrics such as CPU and network, and no memory metrics. It can also scrape Prometheus metrics.

Restricts how resources can be configured, for everyone, including project owners. Policies apply to descendants in the hierarchy. Most are not retroactive, so existing resources that violate them keep working.
Controls SSH access to VMs with IAM roles instead of SSH keys in metadata. roles/compute.osLogin gives login without sudo, and roles/compute.osAdminLogin gives login with sudo.
The highest Customer Care case priority: Critical Impact, Service Unusable in Production. The feature must be GA, with no workaround under 30 minutes. P2 to P4 mean high, medium, and low impact.

A feature that copies full packets, payloads included, from selected VMs to collectors behind an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer. Use it for a third-party IDS or deep forensics. It uses VM bandwidth.

A connection to Google through a service provider, with VLAN attachments that start at 50 Mbps. Use it without colocation presence. Its SLA covers only Google to the provider. Add IPsec for compliance requirements.
A Layer 4 load balancer that delivers packets unchanged, so backends see the client IP address and reply directly to clients. It carries TCP, UDP, and other IP protocols. The backends decrypt TLS.

expansion: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
def: The card data security standard. Every system that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data is in scope, and so are connected systems. Reduce scope with a folder, a separate network, and tokenization.

A Cloud DNS zone that sends queries to the zones of another VPC network. It is one-way and separate from VPC Network Peering. Other networks use it to resolve on-premises names through one forwarding network.
The older Compute Engine block storage. To get more performance, you must increase the disk size. It is not available on the newest machine series, such as N4 and C4.
Health data that HIPAA protects. Keep it in BAA-covered products, and keep it out of resource names, labels, and other metadata, because audit logs can capture metadata.
Data that identifies a person. Sensitive Data Protection finds and de-identifies it, and Data Access audit logs record who reads it.
Recovery of a database to a chosen moment, to undo bad writes or logical corruption. In Cloud SQL, it always creates a new instance. In Spanner, it does not cover a deleted database.
Policy checks inside GKE clusters, as admission control and audit. It is based on Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper and has prebuilt policy bundles. It denies non-compliant configurations in the cluster.
aws: OPA Gatekeeper that you run on Amazon EKS

def: Explains why a principal has, or does not have, a permission. It checks allow and deny policies, but not Cloud Storage ACLs or VPC Service Controls.
A written record of an incident: its impact, the mitigation, the root causes, and the follow-up actions. It is blameless and focuses on processes and tools, not people. Review it and share it widely.
The older version of Spot VMs. They always stop after 24 hours, and Google recommends Spot VMs for new designs.
The Customer Care service for enterprises with priority workloads. P1 cases get a 15-minute initial response target. It includes a named TAM, Customer Aware Support, and Event Management Service.
The default Network Service Tier. Traffic enters Google's network as close as possible to the client. Global external load balancers and Cloud CDN need it. Its SLA is 99.99%.
An IAM policy, attached to a principal set, that limits which resources those principals can access. It fails closed: if IAM cannot evaluate it, IAM blocks access.
A per-subnet setting that lets VMs without external IP addresses reach Google APIs and services. It gives no internet access; use Cloud NAT for that. On-premises hosts use its VIPs over hybrid links.
The Cloud NAT type for traffic to NCC VPC spokes, on-premises, or other clouds. It uses addresses from a PRIVATE_NAT subnet, so it works when subnet ranges overlap.

A private connection to managed services such as Cloud SQL, through VPC Network Peering to a producer network that uses a range you allocate. Peered networks cannot use it, and on-premises hosts need exported custom routes.
A Google API domain with the VIP range 199.36.153.8/30. It allows most Google APIs, whether or not VPC Service Controls supports them. Do not mix it with restricted.googleapis.com.

Gives temporary, on-demand role grants. An entitlement sets who can request which roles, for how long, and if a justification or approval is necessary. The roles end automatically, and audit logs record the access.
Reserved model capacity that you buy with a commitment of 1 week to 1 year, with an SLA. Cover only the steady baseline with it, and send spillover traffic to Standard or Priority PayGo.

A Layer 4 proxy load balancer for TCP, with optional SSL offload in some modes. Backends get the client IP address only through the PROXY protocol. For HTTPS, Google says to use an Application Load Balancer.
A way for proxy Network Load Balancers to give the client IP address to backends. Proxy load balancers do not keep the client IP address in the packet; the X-Forwarded-For header is the other method.
A subnet for the Envoy proxies of regional and cross-region Envoy-based load balancers, and of Secure Web Proxy. Backend firewall rules must allow traffic from this subnet.

A review that checks that a service meets production standards before an SRE team takes responsibility for it. Its phases are engagement, analysis, improvements, training, onboarding, and continuous improvement.
Private access to one published service through an internal IP address in the consumer VPC network. It uses NAT, so the consumer and the producer do not need to coordinate IP ranges.
Replaces sensitive values with cryptographic tokens. Format-preserving tokens can narrow the PCI DSS or HIPAA scope of downstream applications.

The primary source for Google Cloud incidents that affect your projects, including limited-scope incidents. It has a dashboard, an API, and log-based alerts. The public Service Health page shows only broad, severe incidents.
An asynchronous messaging service with at-least-once delivery by default. Publishers know nothing about subscribers, and many subscribers can get each message. Message order needs ordering keys.

The Cloud NAT type for internet egress. It uses external IP addresses that Google allocates or that you assign, for example for partner allowlists. It uses only routes with the default internet gateway as next hop.
A matrix that shows who owns each task. Google recommends one in the migration plan, next to the technical design document and the timeline, when task ownership is unclear.
A pattern that first retrieves the relevant facts, then lets the model generate an answer from them. Use it for private or changing data, because tuning teaches skills, not facts.
A managed RAG framework that ingests, chunks, embeds, indexes, and retrieves your data in a corpus. It supports VPC Service Controls and CMEK, but not data residency.
An SSD-backed zonal read cache for Cloud Storage data that changes rarely and is read often, such as model training data. It also helps multi-region workloads with strict performance needs.
The migration type that changes how the code functions, for example a split of a monolith into microservices. It is more complex than refactor and needs several rounds of testing.
A Cloud SQL copy for read scaling, in the same region or another region. It cannot fail over, but you can promote it to a standalone primary. For replica failover, use an Enterprise Plus DR replica.
The migration type that removes and replaces a workload by a rewrite of the app. Use it when a workload does not meet your goals or costs too much to migrate; it does not suit off-the-shelf software.
The migration type that changes a workload during the move (move and improve). Use it when the architecture is not supported as-is; it takes longer than rehost, and teams must learn new skills.
The migration type that moves a workload as-is (lift and shift). It is the fastest type, and teams keep their tools, but the workload does not use cloud features such as horizontal scaling.
A GKE setting for how fast a cluster gets new versions: Rapid, Regular (the default), Stable, or Extended. To hold a version, use a maintenance exclusion instead of leaving the channel.
The migration type that moves a workload and adds cloud capabilities, for example containers on GKE (lift and optimize). It needs more work and more rounds of testing than rehost.
The migration type that replaces a purchased product with a SaaS product, for example Google Workspace. It takes less effort, but it can cost more and gives less control.
A Google API domain with the VIP range 199.36.153.4/30. It allows only APIs that VPC Service Controls supports and blocks the others, which adds protection against data exfiltration.
The maximum acceptable length of time during which data can be lost. It measures time only. Back up at least as often as the RPO. RPO zero usually needs synchronous replication.
The maximum acceptable time that an application can be offline. A business impact analysis sets it for each application. A smaller RTO costs more, and an RTO in minutes needs automatic recovery.
A federation standard. Google delegates sign-in to an external IdP such as Active Directory through SAML SSO. Workforce Identity Federation and Workload Identity Federation also accept SAML.

A document that lists the contents of a software artifact. Artifact Analysis can generate one in SPDX 2.3 format and store it in Cloud Storage in your project. Assured OSS packages also come with one.

Stores secret values, such as passwords, API keys, and certificates, that a principal with access can read. A rotation schedule only sends Pub/Sub messages, so you write the code that adds the new version.

Tags that IAM controls, which firewall policies use to select VMs. Only holders of the Tag User role can bind them, so app teams cannot change rules by editing a VM. VPC firewall rules cannot use them.

A managed proxy for outbound HTTP and HTTPS. It denies all traffic by default, and allows traffic by source identity, such as a service account or secure tag, and by destination. It logs each request.
Finds misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and threats across projects. The Standard tier has no additional charge. Premium adds threat detection, attack paths, and compliance monitoring.

The Google Cloud service that verifies an external credential against a workload identity pool provider and returns a federated access token. AWS STS AssumeRole maps to service account impersonation instead.

Discovers, inspects, and de-identifies sensitive data, such as PII, across an organization, folder, or project. It includes Cloud DLP. Unlike Amazon Macie, it also masks data and creates reversible tokens.
No single principal has all the permissions for a harmful action. For example, key managers with Cloud KMS Admin do not get the CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter role.

A NEG that connects an Application Load Balancer to Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions, or App Engine. It does not support health checks. Some load balancers offer outlier detection instead. With NEGs in several regions, traffic goes to the closest region.
Connector instances that let serverless code reach a VPC network. They are billed as VMs, have higher latency than Direct VPC egress, and do not scale in after a peak.
A caller gets a short-lived token for a service account and acts as that service account. The caller needs Service Account Token Creator on it, and most audit logs record both identities.

The IAM role (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) that lets a principal impersonate a service account. Grant it on one service account, because on a project it covers every service account in that project.
The IAM role (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) that lets a principal attach a service account to a resource. It does not allow impersonation. Impersonation needs Service Account Token Creator.
The identity that a Google Cloud service uses in your project. For CMEK, the service agent needs the CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter role on the key. The people who create or read the resource do not.

The producer resource that publishes a service through PSC. It points to an internal load balancer forwarding rule or a Secure Web Proxy, and translates consumer traffic with addresses from a PSC NAT subnet.
The VPC Service Controls boundary around projects and their restricted services. A project can be in only one perimeter. Ingress and egress rules allow chosen requests to cross it.

A model in which service projects use subnets of a VPC network in a central host project. Host and service projects must be in the same organization. A central team keeps control of subnets, routes, and firewalls.
A VM option that protects the boot chain with Secure Boot, a vTPM, and integrity monitoring against boot-level and kernel-level malware. It does not protect data in memory; Confidential VM does that.
A contract with customers that has explicit consequences, such as a rebate or a penalty, when a target is missed. A target without explicit consequences is an SLO, not an SLA.

A measure of the service level that users see, usually the ratio of good events to total events, such as the request success ratio. Measure it near the user, not with server metrics such as CPU usage.

The target value for an SLI over a time window, for example 99.9% availability. Set it just reliable enough for user happiness, never 100%. A four-week rolling window is a good general-purpose interval.

A framework that describes threats to source code, builds, and dependencies in the software supply chain. Cloud Build can generate SLSA level 3 build provenance for artifacts that it stores in Artifact Registry.

A change to the source IP address of packets. If GKE Standard Pods use privately used public IPv4 ranges, GKE applies SNAT to Pod-to-Pod traffic. Exclude the cluster ranges from SNAT, or disable default SNAT.
The host name that a client sends at the start of a TLS connection. Without TLS inspection, Cloud NGFW Enterprise URL filtering sees only the domain and SNI of HTTPS traffic.

An audit report on controls for security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, or privacy. Google Cloud issues only Type II reports, which cover a period, and you get them from Compliance Reports Manager.

A Cloud Storage feature that keeps deleted objects and buckets for 7 days by default, up to 90 days. Google recommends it instead of Object Versioning to protect against accidental or malicious deletion.
Physical servers that host only your project's VMs. Use them for physical isolation and for BYOL licenses that count physical cores. You pay for the whole node plus a sole-tenancy premium.

A relational database that scales horizontally and gives external consistency. Multi-region configurations have a 99.999% SLA and need Enterprise Plus edition. Use it for global writes that Cloud SQL cannot give.
A pre-trained API that transcribes audio. Synchronous recognition takes 1 minute or less, batch recognition takes files of up to 480 minutes, and streaming recognition over gRPC handles live audio.
One component whose failure stops the whole service. One large VM can become a SPOF. A global resource survives zone and region outages, but a configuration error can still make it a SPOF.
VMs with discounts of up to 91% that Compute Engine can preempt at any time. They have no SLA and no maximum runtime, and reservations cannot supply them. Use them for fault-tolerant batch work.
Google's approach to operations. SRE teams keep operational work (toil) below 50% of their time, and they spend the error budget on launches and experiments.

A load balancer setting for the minimum TLS version and features between clients and the load balancer. With no SSL policy, the COMPATIBLE profile accepts TLS 1.0. A minimum of TLS 1.3 needs RESTRICTED.
Users authenticate at their identity provider and then use Google Cloud. Google recommends that you disable SSO for super-admin users, or enforce post-SSO verification for them.

The Customer Care service for small to medium organizations with workloads under development. It handles P2 to P4 cases during Hours of Operation. It has no P1 target; its fastest target is 4 hours for P2.
The low-cost Network Service Tier. Traffic enters Google's network near the region of the load balancer. It does not support global external load balancers or Cloud CDN. Its SLA is 99.9%.
A MIG that keeps each VM's name, disks, IP addresses, and metadata when it recreates the VM. It suits databases and legacy monoliths, but it cannot autoscale.

A managed service that copies data into Cloud Storage from Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, HTTP URLs, HDFS, and file systems. File system transfers need agents in your data center, and the service has no SLA.
An automatic Compute Engine discount for a resource that runs more than 25% of a billing month. Only N1, N2, N2D, C2, M1, M2, and sole-tenant nodes get it, and only on self-serve billing accounts.
Tuning a model on labeled examples (about 100 or more) to teach it a new skill, such as classification or entity extraction. Google recommends that you start with prompting and tune only if required.
A named Google contact that only Premium Support includes. The TAM assesses cloud maturity, helps create an adoption roadmap, and gives advice on case priority and escalation.
aws: Technical Account Manager on AWS Enterprise Support

def: The full cost to run a workload, including management work, not only the resource price. A migration TCO also includes data center power, cooling, and maintenance, network use, and the period when both environments run.
The file where Terraform records the resources that it manages. For team use, keep it in the Cloud Storage (gcs) backend, which locks the state. Never edit it by hand, and keep secrets out of it.
A pipeline SDK for Agent Platform Pipelines. Use it only when you process terabytes of structured or text data with TensorFlow; otherwise, use the KFP SDK.
BigQuery access to table data as it was at any time in the last 2 to 7 days (default 7). After that, fail-safe keeps the data 7 more days, and only Cloud Customer Care can recover it.

Work tied to a production service that is manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical, without enduring value, and grows linearly with the service. SRE teams keep operational work below 50% of their time.

Google's ML accelerator. TPU code must compile with XLA, so TPUs fit models where matrix math dominates, not custom operations or dynamic shapes. Use TPUs through Compute Engine, GKE, or Agent Platform.
aws: Amazon EC2 Trn1 and Inf1 instances

def: A device that Google ships to you. You copy data to it and ship it back, and Google uploads the data to Cloud Storage. Use it when an online upload takes more than one week.
A premium option for dual-region Cloud Storage buckets that targets an RPO of 15 minutes for all new objects. It does not work for multi-region buckets.
An approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) engine that scales to billions of vectors. Use it when you build your own retrieval with your own embeddings, or for semantic search and recommendations.
A Vertex AI feature that explains model predictions. Google deprecated it, so do not design new solutions around it.
A pre-trained video analysis API. It is deprecated from September 14, 2026 and shuts down on September 14, 2027. For new designs, Google recommends Gemini video understanding.

A shared IP address for a service. On-premises hosts reach Google APIs through the private.googleapis.com or restricted.googleapis.com VIPs, and Cloud Router must advertise the VIP range with a custom advertisement.
A pre-trained API that analyzes images: labels, faces, landmarks, text, and SafeSearch ratings. Face detection does not identify people. For a scanned-document pipeline, use Document AI instead.

The regional resource that carries traffic between a Cloud Interconnect connection and a VPC network. The multi-region 99.99% topology needs four VLAN attachments in two regions. You can add IPsec encryption only when you create one.
A Compute Engine suite for Patch, OS inventory management, and OS policies. Each VM needs the OS Config agent and an attached service account, and patch jobs skip MIG VMs by default.
A GKE autoscaler that changes the CPU and memory requests of Pods from their usage over time. In Auto mode, it evicts Pods to apply new requests. Do not combine it with the HPA on CPU or memory.

Firewall rules that belong to one VPC network and target all instances, network tags, or service accounts. They have only allow and deny actions, and do not support secure tags or Enterprise features.

Sampled 5-tuple flow records for a network, subnet, VLAN attachment, or VPN tunnel. Use them for monitoring, forensics, and cost analysis. They hold no payloads; Packet Mirroring captures full packets.

A connection between two VPC networks, also across organizations, with full VM bandwidth. It is not transitive, subnet ranges cannot overlap, and network tags and internal DNS names do not work across it.

Puts a perimeter around projects and Google-managed services such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery. It blocks API requests that cross the perimeter, even with valid credentials. Use it together with IAM.
Rules that block web attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Cloud Armor preconfigured WAF rules use the OWASP Core Rule Set. Start at sensitivity level 1 in preview mode, then tune.

Google's principles for cloud design: five core principles, six pillars (operational excellence; security, privacy, and compliance; reliability; cost optimization; performance optimization; sustainability), and two perspectives (AI and ML, and financial services).
A serverless orchestrator that chains HTTP-based services, with YAML or JSON definitions, millisecond latency, and billing per step. A workflow can wait for up to a year.
Lets employees and partners from an OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP sign in to Google Cloud with SSO. It stores no user accounts in Google Cloud, so you do not need Google Cloud Directory Sync.
Lets a workload outside Google Cloud exchange its own credential, such as an AWS credential or a GitHub OIDC token, for a short-lived Google token. It removes the need for service account keys.

Lets IAM treat a Kubernetes ServiceAccount as a principal, so GKE workloads call Google Cloud APIs without keys. All clusters in one project share one workload identity pool, so the same namespace and ServiceAccount get the same access.
aws: EKS Pod Identity or IAM roles for service accounts

def: A container for the providers that Workload Identity Federation trusts. Create one pool for each environment, and manage pools and providers in a dedicated project.

A form of immutability: after you write data, no one can change or delete it. Backup vaults in Backup and DR Service enforce it, so backups stay recoverable after ransomware attacks or accidental deletion.
The compiler that all code for TPUs must compile with. JAX and PyTorch code compile with it. Models with custom operations in the training loop fit GPUs better.
